summary: Semantic tags name the parts of a page: header, nav, main, article, aside, and footer. They look like plain boxes, but screen readers and search engines use them to understand the page.
notes: Screen reader users can jump straight to <nav> or <main>, so they skip content they do not need.
Use <main> once per page, for the content that is not repeated on every page.
<article> is for content that would make sense alone. <section> is for a themed part of a page with its own heading.
pitfall: Building the whole page out of <div> elements with class names like "header". It looks the same but gives assistive technology nothing to work with.
